The factors are treated as correlated in this synthesis, so the posterior reflects a combined, calibrated uplift rather than a simple additive sum. No further calibration adjustments beyond acknowledging correlation were applied.

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed presence of the riot-control agent CS in multiple front-line incidents in Ukraine
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW analyses confirmed CS in front-line samples from multiple incidents (Nov 2024 and Apr 2025), indicating ongoing battlefield use by a state actor and elevating near-term risk (OPCW 2024Nov; OPCW 2025Apr).

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence assessments that Russia has intensified use of banned chemical weapons in Ukraine
causal-factors.rationale: Dutch and German intelligence publicly assert that Russia has expanded or normalized the use of chloropicrin and CS, signaling higher likelihood of further incidents (AP News 2025Jul; Al Jazeera 2025Jul).

causal-factors.name: Analyses projecting continued Russian chemical weapons use in Europe over 5-10 years
causal-factors.rationale: Think-tank projections (Atlantic Council, 2025) argue Russia is likely to continue chemical weapon use in Europe, sustaining near-term risk for Ukraine before 2026 (5-10 years).

causal-factors.name: Deterrence and allied readiness potentially raising costs for use
causal-factors.rationale: Credible deterrence by the United States and Europe increases costs for Russia and reduces the probability of chemical weapons use in Ukraine (Atlantic Council 2025).

causal-factors.name: Uncertainty about attribution and ongoing investigations
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW findings identify CS presence but do not attribute culpability, leaving attribution uncertain and limiting certainty about near-term actions (OPCW 2024Nov; OPCW 2025Apr).

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed CS detections along front lines (Nov 2024, Feb 2025, Jun 2025)
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW laboratory analyses confirmed CS presence in multiple front-line incidents, indicating active deployment of riot-control agents in combat.

causal-factors.name: Credible intelligence indicating Russia's stepped-up use of banned chemical weapons (chloropicrin and CS) and normalization
causal-factors.rationale: Dutch and German intelligence assessments describe sustained, standardized use of chemical agents by Russia in Ukraine, signaling higher likelihood of at least episodic state-actor deployment.

causal-factors.name: Attribution uncertainty about the actor
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW findings do not specify the perpetrator, which maintains uncertainty and realism about the actor while not eliminating the underlying risk.

causal-factors.name: Deterrence and international norms
causal-factors.rationale: Strong normative prohibitions against chemical weapons and potential costs from sanctions and allied responses could suppress additional uses.

causal-factors.name: War dynamics and escalation pressure on Russian leadership
causal-factors.rationale: If Moscow perceives strategic value in escalating to blunt Ukrainian resistance, chemical weapons could be employed as a force-multiplier on future fronts.

causal-factors.name: OPCW-confirmed presence of riot-control agent CS in Ukraine along front lines (Nov 2024 first TAV; Oct 2024 incidents; Feb 2025 second TAV; Jun 2025 third TAV)
causal-factors.rationale: Laboratory-confirmed CS detections across multiple incidents along the front lines indicate established chemical-agent use by a state actor, elevating near-term risk of another incident.

causal-factors.name: Intelligence assessments by Dutch and German agencies of increased Russian use of banned chemical weapons (chloropicrin and CS)
causal-factors.rationale: Public intelligence assessments of intensified usage imply higher likelihood of a future incident, assuming ongoing operational conditions.

causal-factors.name: Attribution uncertainty about the perpetrator despite CS detections
causal-factors.rationale: OPCW findings focus on presence, not attribution; uncertainty reduces forecast confidence and can bias the probability either way.

causal-factors.name: OPCW monitoring and international oversight and deterrence potential (assistance, sanctions, and compliance signaling)
causal-factors.rationale: Ongoing monitoring and deterrence increase costs of use and reduce the probability of successful, undetected chemical-weapons incidents.

causal-factors.name: Prolonged Ukraine conflict and front-line escalation pressures could incentivize use in some scenarios
causal-factors.rationale: Continued combat intensity and innovative tactics can raise incentives for chemical-weapons employment as a force multiplier.

synthesis: The CS detections and credible intel imply non-trivial risk of state-actor chemical weapon use in Ukraine before May 2026, but attribution uncertainty and deterrence justify a modest downward calibration from the ensemble. The result is a 60% central estimate with a 50–70% plausible range.
